source: Dallas City Code ch. 51P, Article 946 (City Attorney's codified article, April 2026)

sections.title: Legislative History
sections.text:
SEC. 51P-946.101. LEGISLATIVE HISTORY.

PD 946 was established by Ordinance No. 29936, passed by the Dallas City Council on November 10, 2015. (Ord. 29936)

sections.title: Property Location And Size
sections.text:
SEC. 51P-946.102. PROPERTY LOCATION AND SIZE.

PD 946 is established on property located at the northeast corner of Preston Road and Northwest Highway. The size of PD 946 is approximately 2.02 acres. (Ord. 29936)

sections.title: Definitions And Interpretations
sections.text:
SEC. 51P-946.103. DEFINITIONS AND INTERPRETATIONS.

(a) Unless otherwise stated, the definitions and interpretations in Chapter 51A apply to this article. In this article, NONFUNCTIONING BALCONY means an architectural feature that does not have a horizontal landing area and is not accessible from a dwelling unit.

(b) Unless otherwise stated, all references to articles, divisions, or sections in this article are to articles, divisions, or sections in Chapter 51A.

(c) This district is considered to be a residential zoning district. (Ord. 29936)

sections.title: Exhibits
sections.text:
SEC. 51P-946.104. EXHIBITS.

The following exhibits are incorporated into this article:

(1) Exhibit 946A: development plan.

(2) Exhibit 946B: landscape plan. (Ord. 29936)

sections.title: Development Plan
sections.text:
SEC. 51P-946.105. DEVELOPMENT PLAN.

Development and use of the Property must comply with the development plan (Exhibit 946A). If there is a conflict between the text of this article and the development plan, the text of this article controls. (Ord. 29936)

sections.title: Minor Amendment To Development Plan
sections.text:
SEC. 51P-946.106. MINOR AMENDMENT TO DEVELOPMENT PLAN.

(a) In general. Except as provided in this section, amendments to a development plan must comply with Section 51A-4.702(h), as amended.

(b) Multifamily use. The director may approve minor amendments to the courtyard shown on the development plan following the director’s procedure outlined in Section 51A-4.702(h), except that the provision requiring that the proposed development plan not have residential adjacency does not apply. (Ord. 29936)

sections.title: Main Uses Permitted
sections.text:
SEC. 51P-946.107. MAIN USES PERMITTED.

The only main uses permitted are those main uses permitted in the MF-1(A) Multifamily District, subject to the same conditions applicable in the MF-1(A) Multifamily District, as set out in Chapter 51A. For example, a use permitted in the MF-1(A) Multifamily District only by specific use permit (SUP) is permitted in this district only by SUP; a use subject to development impact review (DIR) in the MF-1(A) Multifamily District is subject to DIR in this district; etc. (Ord. 29936)

sections.title: Accessory Uses
sections.text:
SEC. 51P-946.108. ACCESSORY USES.

(a) As a general rule, an accessory use is permitted in any district in which the main use is permitted. Some specific accessory uses, however, due to their unique nature, are subject to additional regulations in Section 51A-4.217. For more information regarding accessory uses, consult Section 51A- 4.217.

(b) The following accessory uses are not permitted:

-- Accessory outside display of merchandise. -- Accessory outside sales. -- Accessory pathological waste incinerator. (Ord. 29936)

sections.title: Yard, Lot, And Space Regulations
Off-Street Parking And Loading
sections.text:
SEC. 51P-946.110. OFF-STREET PARKING AND LOADING.

(a) In general. Except as provided in this section, consult the use regulations in Division 51A-4.200 for the specific off-street parking and loading requirements for each use.

(b) Multifamily use.

(1) In addition to the off-street parking required in Division 51A-4.200, guest parking must be provided at a ratio of 0.2 spaces per dwelling unit.

(2) All off-street parking must be located within an aboveground or underground parking structure. (Ord. 29936)

sections.title: Roadway Improvements
sections.text:
SEC. 51P-946.111. ROADWAY IMPROVEMENTS.

Before the issuance of a certificate of occupancy for a multifamily use, a left-turn lane from southbound Preston Road onto eastbound Averill Way must be provided with final design and construction to be approved by the Texas Department of Transportation. (Ord. 29936)

sections.title: Environmental Performance Standards
sections.text:
SEC. 51P-946.112. ENVIRONMENTAL PERFORMANCE STANDARDS.

See Article VI. (Ord. 29936)

sections.title: Landscaping
sections.text:
SEC. 51P-946.113. LANDSCAPING.

(a) In general. Except as provided in this section, landscaping must be provided in accordance with Article X.

(b) Multifamily use.

(1) Landscaping must be provided as shown on the landscape plan (Exhibit 946B).

(2) Each required tree must have a minimum caliper of four inches at time of planting, measured at a point 12 inches above the root ball.

(c) Maintenance. Plant materials must be maintained in a healthy, growing condition. (Ord. 29936)

sections.title: Design Standards For Multifamily Uses
sections.text:
SEC. 51P-946.114. DESIGN STANDARDS FOR MULTIFAMILY USES.

(a) Masonry facade. Facades facing an improved public right-of-way must be at least 80 percent masonry, excluding windows, entrances, and ingress and egress points. Masonry includes stone, brick, concrete, hollow clay tile, decorative concrete blocks or tile, glass block, other similar building materials, or a combination of these materials. For purposes of this provision, stucco is considered masonry but Exterior Finish Insulations System (EFIS) materials are not.

(b) Facade wall changes. Facade walls must have one or more of the following changes:

(1) A minimum of two changes of color, texture, or material, either diagonally, horizontally, or vertically, at intervals of not less than five feet and not more than 20 feet.

(2) Changes in plane with a depth of at least 12 inches, either diagonally, horizontally, or vertically, for each 50 feet of street facing facade.

(c) Balconies. Any balcony located within the dimensional area labeled as East Facade 1, East Facade 2, and East Facade 3 on the development plan must be a nonfunctioning balcony.

(d) Pedestrian amenities. A minimum of two of each of the following pedestrian amenities must be provided along an improved public right-of-way:

(1) benches,

(2) trash receptacles, and

(3) bicycle racks.

(e) Masonry wall.

(1) A minimum eight-foot-high solid masonry wall must be provided along the eastern Property line.

(2) Access through the wall is limited to emergency access only with final design and location to be approved by the fire marshal.

(3) A masonry wall is not required along the eastern Property line if the adjacent property to the east is developed with a density of 28 dwelling units or more.

(f) Fences. If fences facing a public right-of-way are provided, they must be constructed to be a minimum of 50 percent open.

(g) Rooftop patios. Rooftop patios are not permitted within the easternmost 35 feet of the Property. (Ord. 29936)

sections.title: Sidewalks
sections.text:
SEC. 51P-946.115. SIDEWALKS.

(a) Sidewalks must be a minimum width of six feet with an unobstructed width of four feet. ADA approved tree well grates are considered part of the unobstructed width.

(b) Design and construction of sidewalks must provide a continuous path for a pedestrian across private drives. (Ord. 29936)

sections.title: Signs
sections.text:
SEC. 51P-946.116. SIGNS.

Signs must comply with the provisions for non-business zoning districts in Article VII. (Ord. 29936)

sections.title: Additional Provisions
sections.text:
SEC. 51P-946.117. ADDITIONAL PROVISIONS.

(a) The Property must be properly maintained in a state of good repair and neat appearance.

(b) Development and use of the Property must comply with all federal and state laws and regulations, and with all ordinances, rules, and regulations of the city. (Ord. 29936)

sections.title: Compliance With Conditions
sections.text:
SEC. 51P-946.118. COMPLIANCE WITH CONDITIONS.

(a) All paved areas, permanent drives, streets, and drainage structures, if any, must be constructed in accordance with standard city specifications, and completed to the satisfaction of the city.

(b) The building official shall not issue a building permit to authorize work, or a certificate of occupancy to authorize the operation of a use, until there has been full compliance with this article, the Dallas Development Code, the construction codes, and all other ordinances, rules, and regulations of the city. (Ord. 29936)
